investigate: Inadequate ==access to laboratory resources== in remote secondary schools hinders efficient chemistry learning.
The study investigates the effectiveness of integrating ==virtual and augmented reality (VR/AR)== into project-based chemistry learning.
In a quasi-experiment, 32 upper-secondary students engaged in ==VR/AR-supported environmental chemistry projects==, while 32 received conventional instruction.
find: The experimental group showed ==substantially greater achievement gains== than the control group (mean gains of 19 versus 3).
Experimental students also showed ==increases in motivation and perceived understanding==, two measures that were strongly positively related.
The authors suggest VR/AR-supported projects may be ==a promising approach== for chemistry education in resource-constrained rural contexts.

caption.question: Can virtual and augmented reality help rural students learn chemistry with limited laboratory resources?
caption.intro: Nailya Shertayeva, Bibigul Shagrayeva, Yerman Shertayev, Akkongyr Zhylysbayeva and Elmira Amirbekova test **VR/AR-supported project-based chemistry learning** with 64 upper-secondary students in rural Kazakhstan.

source_notes.investigate: Background; Purpose; Sample and Design and methods (64 students, 32 per group; VR/AR-supported environmental chemistry projects vs conventional instruction).
source_notes.find: Results: mean gain 19 vs 3 (Cohen's d = 0.89 not shown); increases in motivation and perceived understanding; strong positive relationship between them (r = 0.68). Conclusion: 'may be a promising pedagogical approach' in resource-constrained rural contexts.
